title: DRC Ebola Toll Passes 3,000 Deaths as Confirmed Cases Reach 6,186
detail: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ministry of Health reported 6,186 confirmed cases and 3,007 deaths (crude CFR ~48.6%) as of 31 August 2026, per the ECDC's Ebola outbreak tracker (updated 2 September) — a rise of 86 confirmed cases and 57 deaths since the 31 August report, with new cases concentrated in Ituri (49), North Kivu (32) and Haut-Uélé (5). Ituri province remains the epicenter with 5,065 cases and 2,305 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones, while North Kivu has recorded 868 cases and 589 deaths across 15 of 34 health zones. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus and declared a PHEIC on 17 May, has now killed more than 3,000 people in under four months — surpassing the death toll of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak (2,299) by a wide margin and remaining the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic ever recorded. As of the update, 1,409 patients have recovered and 830 remain hospitalized in isolation, with 88% of identified contacts under active follow-up across 60 of 151 health zones in six provinces. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said international attention, political focus and resources 'are still lagging behind the reality unfolding on the ground.'

sources.name: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control

media.caption: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 3,000 deaths as confirmed cases climb to 6,186

title: WHO Chief Warns of Unknown Transmission Chains, Appeals for $1.3 Billion as DRC Deaths Pass 3,000
detail: WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told a media briefing on 2 September 2026 that the DRC's Ebola response must be scaled up urgently, warning that up to 80% of new cases are appearing outside known contact lists — 'that means there are chains of transmission we don't know about,' he said, adding, 'until every chain is found and broken, the epidemic will continue; and it will continue to pose a threat to DRC, its neighbours, and the region.' Tedros appealed for accelerated funding toward the DRC government's six-month, $1.3 billion response plan, acknowledging the request comes 'at a time when financing for humanitarian assistance has contracted, and when there are many other competing priorities,' but said 'we can control this epidemic if we choose to.' WHO said it has deployed over 300 experts and 330 tonnes of supplies, expanded lab capacity from 1 to 24 facilities (3,000 tests/day), and grown treatment-bed capacity to 1,300 across 49 facilities, with plans to triple beds to 3,000 within three months. In Bunia, residents described daily life slowing to a crawl under the outbreak: 'I had to flee the area because of the danger looming over us,' said resident Jean-Claude Angwanzia, while transport driver Papy Baraka said, 'The disease puts everyone at risk ... We are afraid.'

media.caption: Health workers bury the coffin of Neema Minaro, 66, who died of Ebola, in Bunia, DRC, 2 September 2026
